title: Vice-President flags off Har Ghar Tiranga Bike Rally of MPs, commemorating 150 years of Vande Mataram
subtitle:
Har Ghar Tiranga has become a People's Movement , It Gives Visible Form to the Spirit of Vande Mataram: Vice-President
Vande Mataram transformed love for the motherland into a national duty: Vice President
body_text:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today flagged off the Har Ghar Tiranga Bike Rally with Members of Parliament and other public representatives at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, commemorating 150 years of the National Song, Vande Mataram.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan flagged off a special Bike Rally with Members of Parliament as part of #HarGharTiranga 2026, organised by the Ministry of Culture, commemorating the 150th anniversary of our National Song, ‘Vande Mataram’. Union Ministers Shri Kiren… pic.twitter.com/MeN5LOCQRt — Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) August 12, 2026
The rally proceeded from Bharat Mandapam to Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, carrying the message of national pride, unity and citizen participation.
Addressing the gathering, he said Vande Mataram transformed love for the motherland into a national duty and became a powerful expression of the spirit of India's freedom struggle. He recalled how its immortal words inspired countless freedom fighters with courage, sacrifice and hope.
Recalling his recent visit to the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, the Vice-President said his visit to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island and the historic Cellular Jail had been deeply moving. He recalled Netaji's hoisting of the Tricolour in 1943 and the sacrifices of freedom fighters imprisoned in Cellular Jail, many of whom went to the gallows with the cry of Vande Mataram.
Highlighting the nationwide impact of the National Song, Vande Mataram, in India’s freedom struggle, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan recalled the contributions and sacrifices of freedom fighters and leaders from Tamil Nadu, including V. O. Chidambaram Pillai, Subramaniya Siva, Tiruppur Kumaran and Vanchinathan, as well as national poet Subramania Bharati, who carried the spirit and message of Vande Mataram to the people.
The Vice-President said the Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan, launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in 2022, has evolved into a people's movement, with citizens participating in Tiranga Yatras, bike and cycle rallies, cultural programmes and other activities. He said the Tricolour gives a visible form to the feeling of one Motherland and urged MPs and public representatives to promote the campaign in their constituencies and inspire citizens to hoist the National Flag with pride.
Union Ministers Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Shri Virendra Kumar, Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Shri Kiren Rijiju and Shri Jitendra Singh along with Members of Parliament, and other public representatives, participated in the rally.

enrichment.summary: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan flagged off a Har Ghar Tiranga Bike Rally with Members of Parliament at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, marking 150 years of the National Song 'Vande Mataram'. The rally, organised by the Ministry of Culture, proceeded to the Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium as part of the Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan 2026. The Vice-President spoke about Vande Mataram's role in inspiring freedom fighters and highlighted contributions of Tamil Nadu freedom fighters like V.O. Chidambaram Pillai and Subramania Bharati.
enrichment.context:
Vande Mataram, composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and included in his 1882 novel Anandamath, became a rallying cry during India's freedom struggle after being sung at the 1896 Indian National Congress session. It was adopted as the National Song of India (distinct from the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana) by the Constituent Assembly in 1950. 2026 marks 150 years since its composition, making this a significant commemorative year for the government's cultural and nationalist outreach programmes.

The Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan, launched by PM Modi in 2022 as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav commemorations, encourages citizens to hoist the national flag at their homes around Independence Day to foster patriotism and civic participation. It has since become an annual feature around 15 August, with government functionaries organising rallies, yatras and cultural events to sustain public engagement. Such commemorations also serve to reinforce collective memory of the freedom struggle, including lesser-highlighted regional contributions such as those of Tamil Nadu revolutionaries mentioned in this release.

prelims_questions.question: The National Song 'Vande Mataram' was composed by which of the following personalities?
prelims_questions.explanation: Vande Mataram was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and first appeared in his novel Anandamath (1882); it was formally adopted as India's National Song by the Constituent Assembly in 1950.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Har Ghar Tiranga' Abhiyan was launched in which year as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav commemorations?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states the Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2022 and has since evolved into a people's movement.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of the National Song 'Vande Mataram' in mobilising mass participation during India's freedom struggle, with reference to regional contributions such as those from Tamil Nadu.
